open_points.subject: A04 Required test 11 — Customer erasure
open_points.text: for a Customer a correction, restricting and lifting, ending and resuming the relationship, and erasure (M04) — moves the record's revision by exactly one and sets its last-changed instant to the current instant
open_points.question: Does Customer erasure remove its revision and last-changed instant, as A04 rules 1 and 3, A04-4 and M04 require, or does it retain and advance them as Required test 11 requires?
options: Remove Customer erasure from the actions that advance and retain revision and last-changed instant; test instead that erasure leaves no revision or last-changed instant.
Change the erasure result so it retains a revision advanced by one and a last-changed instant set to the current instant.
open_points.default_guess: Remove erasure from this list and show A04-4 for it, because the accepted model says an erased Customer keeps neither revision nor last-changed instant.

witness.initial: A Customer has revision 7, a last-changed instant, and unerased contact data.
events: The owner erases the Customer's contact data while stating revision 7.
outcomes: A04-4 and M04: the erased Customer has no revision and no last-changed instant.
A04 Required test 11: the Customer has revision 8 and its last-changed instant is the current instant.
witness.observer: The owner reading the erased Customer, and the Factory check for A04-3/A04-4.

open_points.subject: A04 current-instant reading
open_points.text: sets its last-changed instant to the current instant
open_points.question: How many UTC wall-clock readings does one accepted operation take, and which reading is the “current instant” written as the record's last-changed instant?
options: Take one UTC wall-clock reading for the whole operation and reuse it for every instant that operation writes.
Take one reading specifically when applying the record mutation.
Permit separate readings for the record, audit entry and other effects of the same operation.
open_points.default_guess: Take one UTC wall-clock reading per operation and reuse it for all instants written by that operation.

witness.initial: The supplied UTC clock returns 10:00:00 on its first read and 10:00:01 on its second read.
events: The owner submits an accepted Customer correction.
The operation writes the Customer's last-changed instant and its audit entry.
outcomes: A single operation reading makes both instants 10:00:00.
Separate readings make the Customer instant 10:00:00 and the audit instant 10:00:01, or the reverse depending on read order.
witness.observer: A test or owner reading both the Customer and its audit entry.

open_points.subject: A04-6 and Required test 11
open_points.text: each such action that changes nothing (A05) leaves both where they were. Shows A04-3, A04-6.
open_points.question: Must A04-6 formally guarantee that an unchanged action preserves both revision and last-changed instant, or must Required test 11 stop claiming that its two-field assertion shows A04-6?
options: Extend A04-6 to state both r.revision' = r.revision and r.last_changed' = r.last_changed.
Keep A04-6 about revision only and bind the last-changed assertion to a separate invariant.
open_points.default_guess: Extend A04-6 to include the unchanged last-changed instant, matching the normative rules and Required test 11.

open_points.subject: A21 security review after the A04 change
open_points.text: A change to a decision a category names reopens this review.
open_points.question: What are the recorded outcomes of the reopened authorization and concurrency reviews after this change to A04, which both categories name?
options: Record that authorization and concurrency were reviewed again and that no outcome or reference changed.
Record the changed outcomes or references found by the reopened review.
open_points.default_guess: Keep A21 reopened until authorization and concurrency are reviewed and their outcomes are recorded.

witness.initial: A21 is closed, and its authorization and concurrency categories both reference A04.
events: A04 Required test 11 is changed after the latest recorded A21 review.
No later security-review entry records review of that A04 change.
outcomes: A21 rule 2 reopens the review and closure waits for recorded category outcomes.
A later agent silently treats a Required-tests-only change as exempt and leaves A21 closed.
witness.observer: The State 2 gate and the security reviewer.

open_points.subject: SIGN_IN_REFUSAL_LIMIT delivery path
open_points.text:
the five refusals of rule 3 are
   `SIGN_IN_REFUSAL_LIMIT`
open_points.rule:
Таблица выше —
исчерпывающий список путей значения, и у каждого из них своя форма: перечисление
называется адресом, константа поставщика — `the imported X constant`,
настройка — полем объекта настроек.
open_points.question: The passage must identify five through the prescribed imported-constant path, for example as “the imported `SIGN_IN_REFUSAL_LIMIT` constant”, rather than naming the symbol alone.

open_points.subject: contract that supplies the current instant
open_points.text: a datetime parameter, a clock port in __init__, or a declared authority module
open_points.question: Which exact contract form supplies the decided time source to each mutating operation that writes a fresh timestamp?
options: A datetime parameter supplied on each call.
A clock port supplied in the module or service constructor.
A declared authority module used by the mutating operation.
open_points.default_guess: Use an injected clock port so one operation can take and share one reading while tests replace the clock.
consequences: A datetime parameter makes the caller choose the operation's instant and requires every caller contract to carry it.
A constructor clock port centralizes clock authority and supports deterministic replacement in tests.
A declared authority module reduces call signatures but introduces an implicit module-level dependency.
open_points.requirement: every mutating operation that writes a fresh timestamp receives the time source State 2 decided, in its contract (a datetime parameter, a clock port in __init__, or a declared authority module)
